bank_plan.formula: (lesson_check_items + module_check_items) x 2 alternates + forms x form_length
bank_plan.eighty_twenty_note: 80% instruction / 20% assessment honoured at course level (I+A=T); bank serves lesson checks, module checks, 3 practice forms and a protected final.
bank_plan.size_band_note: Planning range per assessment standard (200-600 skills; 600-1500+ large certification). This is a planning guide, not proof of quality.

mcq_limitation_note: NCLEX includes alternate and next-generation clinical-judgment item formats; Mastemy uses MCQ/MR only and does not replicate clinical performance.

items.stem: A practical nurse notices a client's blood pressure has dropped sharply and the client is dizzy. What is the priority action?

options.text: Protect the client from falling and notify the supervising RN
options.rationale: Correct: ensure safety and escalate, since assessment and orders exceed the practical-nurse scope here.
Prescribing is outside the practical-nurse scope.

options.text: Document and reassess at the next scheduled round
options.rationale: An acute change needs immediate action, not delay.

options.text: Reassure the client it is nothing to worry about

items.explanation: Keep the client safe and report an acute change to the RN within scope.
items.provenance: AI-drafted original item, not from any proprietary, leaked or paid exam source

items.stem: Which task is appropriate to delegate to unlicensed assistive personnel?

options.text: Assisting a stable client with bathing
options.rationale: Correct: routine hygiene for a stable client is within assistive-personnel scope.
Initial assessment is a licensed responsibility.
IV medication is outside assistive-personnel scope.
Care planning is a licensed nursing responsibility.

items.explanation: Routine, stable-client hygiene is delegable; assessment, IV meds and planning are not.
items.provenance: AI-drafted original item, not from any proprietary, leaked or paid exam source

items.stem: Which TWO observations should a practical nurse report promptly to the supervising RN?

options.text: A new onset of confusion in a previously alert client
options.rationale: Correct: an acute mental-status change needs prompt escalation.

options.text: A wound with new purulent drainage and spreading redness
options.rationale: Correct: signs of infection require escalation.

options.text: A client sleeping comfortably through the night
options.rationale: Normal rest does not require escalation.

options.text: A client eating a full breakfast
Stable vital signs within the client's baseline
options.rationale: Baseline stable signs do not require reporting.

items.explanation: Acute changes such as new confusion or infection signs must be reported; normal findings need not.
